title: Сотейник в сейфе  (The Sauté Pan in the Safe)

segments.t: Back in the office at Claude Monet, German takes kitchen security to a ridiculous extreme by locking the copper sauté pan inside a heavy metal safe and pocketing the key.
Вам не кажется, что это перебор?
От него можно ожидать чего угодно.
Я всё-таки возьму ключики от сейфа.
Он не станет заниматься такой ерундой.
Let's go through Vika and German's exchange around the office safe.
'And your sauté pan is fine.' Vika aims the remark beside German: notice how Russian needs no word for "am", "is", or "are" in the present — placing the words side by side says it all.
Вам не кажется, что это перебор?
'Does it not seem to you that this is overkill?' Vika questions evenly before German can change the subject.
'He steals a defenseless sauté pan!' German reaches for this vivid detail in reply: "bezzashchitnyy" means "defenseless", and it carries the main weight of what German is saying.
'And these are security measures.' German hands over the thought for Vika: notice how Russian needs no word for "am", "is", or "are" in the present — placing the words side by side says it all.
'Excuse me, what safe is this?' German probes wryly as Vika tries to explain the situation.
'It was left over from the old owners.' Vika underscores one vivid touch with German: "khozyayev" means "owner, proprietor" (from "khozyain"), giving the line its exact edge.
'I do not use it.' Vika delivers that line facing German: the "-sya" ending on "polzuyus" ("I am taking advantage") turns the action inward or makes it happen between people naturally.
'Well, I will use it, give me the keys.' German opens up calmly facing Vika, testing Vika's reaction in the middle of the exchange.
'Now that is another matter.' German picks one classic term toward Vika: "drugoye" means "another, other" (from "drugoy"), giving the line its exact edge.

'Do you think Viktor will try again?' Vika phrases that thought at once: Russian keeps the exact word order of a normal statement here, turning it into a question for German purely through rising pitch at the end.
От него можно ожидать чего угодно.
'You can expect anything at all from him.' German opens up evenly to be clear, grounding the moment in plain reality.
Я всё-таки возьму ключики от сейфа.
'I will take the spare keys to the safe after all.' Vika colors one key expression toward German: "klyuchiki" means "little key" (from "klyuchik"), giving the line its exact edge.

'You do not use it, do you?' German hands over this point beside Vika: the "-sya" ending on "polzuyetes" ("are taking advantage of") turns the action inward or makes it happen between people naturally.
Он не станет заниматься такой ерундой.
'He will not bother with such nonsense.' Vika responds calmly to be clear, bringing things back to earth after the buildup. Now let's hear the whole scene again from start to finish.
Вам не кажется, что это перебор?
От него можно ожидать чего угодно.
Я всё-таки возьму ключики от сейфа.
Он не станет заниматься такой ерундой.
That wraps up this scene as german locks the reclaimed copper sauté pan inside an old office safe to keep Barinov away from it, and Vika slyly asks to borrow the spare keys. See you next time!
